title: Decide the fate of the other two Phase 1 drift surfaces
description:
Phase 1 converted FOUR compiler-enforced agreements into comment-enforced ones. The collect vocabulary is its own tick (the dangerous one). These are the other two, and the honest answer for either may be 'leave it'.

1. THE EIGHT-COLOUR PALETTE. internal/factory/dashboard/view.go carries copies of eight hex values from internal/styles (verified identical: #F38BA8, #A6E3A1, #94E2D5, #89DCEB, #CBA6F7, #F5C2E7, #A6ADC8, #7F849C). The copy's own comment argues the two products SHOULD be free to diverge — ticfac's dashboard is its own surface and binding two products' visual identity together is a coupling neither wants. If that reasoning holds, this needs NO contract and the right outcome is to record that and close it. Do not add a fixture just because you can.

2. THE HERD DASHBOARD KEY BINDINGS. A test used to render the herd board's real footer and compare bindings, so a rebinding there failed the factory build. It did not survive the import removal; the keys are now a frozen literal (herdBoardKeys) and both view_test.go and doc.go say plainly that the agreement is now human-carried. The 82h review called this the weakest point in the Phase 1 diff and correctly labelled. Unlike the palette, this one is a UX consistency claim that a user would notice breaking — two boards in the same product family with different keys.

FOR EACH: decide contract / leave-it, and write the reasoning where a reader lands on it. The bar for adding a fixture is that drift would cause a real problem someone notices — not that drift is possible.
acceptance_criteria: Both surfaces have an explicit decision recorded at the site, not left implicit. Any surface that gets a contract has a fixture read by both sides and a demonstrated failure on drift. Any surface deliberately left uncontracted says so and says why. go test ./... green.
